attributed: The effective sample size can be computed from the autocorrelation function, as in Afyouni et al. 2019 (cited for the method behind the reporting recommendation).
note: Afyouni et al. review effective-degrees-of-freedom estimators computed from the autocorrelation function: Bartlett 1935 for AR(1) (Eq. 6), Quenouille 1947 (Eq. 7), its global form (Eq. 8) and Bayley–Hammersley (Eq. 9), all derived under zero cross-correlation. text_at_d108d66: Outside the pre-specified TR range (0.72 s) and deconvolved in the primary analysis; listed as the source study. At the operating point of its stated band and TR (0.008–0.09 Hz at 0.72 s: ideal-band-pass r₁ ≈ 0.97) the map gives ∂sts/∂r₁ = 32.8 against ∂rtr/∂r₁ = 0.06 (Table B item 1), so a regional gradient of BOLD lag-1 autocorrelation would produce a synergy-minus-redundancy gradient of the same spatial form. The study's own phase-randomised surrogate is the one test of that exposure in this table: on the family it sits on the q = 0 line, where sts = 2 min(S_x, S_y) and rtr = 0, so the surrogate gradient is, up to noise, the regional r₁ gradient; its correlations with the macroscale maps were 0.09, 0.01, 0.17, 0.21, 0.26 and −0.16 (only glycolytic index, ρ = 0.26, spin p = 0.028, significant) against 0.40, 0.48, 0.22, 0.28, 0.40 and 0.54 for the observed gradient (Table 1, p. 10). That argues against the exposure for those macroscale associations on that dataset; the correlation of the observed gradient with regional r₁, which this repository measures on its own data (+0.792 for sts − rtr), is not reported there. Whether the gradient coincides with the fMRI timescale hierarchy (Raut et al. 2020, read: intrinsic timescales lengthen from unimodal to transmodal cortex, p. 20891) is not tested in either paper.
attributed: Luppi 2022 used TR 0.72 s and 0.008–0.09 Hz with HRF deconvolution in the primary analysis; its phase-randomised surrogate gradient correlated with the macroscale maps at 0.09, 0.01, 0.17, 0.21, 0.26 and −0.16 (only GI significant) against 0.40, 0.48, 0.22, 0.28, 0.40 and 0.54 for the observed gradient (Table 1); it reports no correlation of the gradient with regional r₁ and no test against the timescale hierarchy.
note: The reading itself is the paper's own inference. The r₁ ≈ 0.97, both derivatives, the q = 0 argument and the +0.792 are the paper's computations, not the work's. The facts about the work hold: TR 0.72 s, 0.008–0.09 Hz and deconvolution in the primary analysis (pp. 13–14); a phase-randomised surrogate with exactly the six stated correlations and only GI significant (Pspin = 0.028; Table 1 is uncorrected); and the observed values 0.40, 0.48, 0.22, 0.28, 0.40 and 0.54. The work reports no correlation of its gradient with regional autocorrelation, and 'timescale' occurs nowhere in it. The Raut et al. 2020 content belongs to that unit.
